findings.claim: Generated code targeting .NET Framework or .NET Standard 2.0 still has no ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute because every template disables it under NETFRAMEWORK or NETSTANDARD2_0. The attribute is available on both targets, so these guards leave supported targets outside the requirement that all generated code be decorated.

receipt_plan.detail: Run ResolverRetainsExcludeFromCodeCoverageOnFrameworksWhereItExists for NETFRAMEWORK and NETSTANDARD2_0. Generate a resolver with those preprocessor symbols and assert that the resolver symbol has ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute; on head the conditional compilation removes it in both cases.

findings.claim: The MessagePackSecurity copy constructor no longer copies HashCollisionResistant. For example, copying MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData (or calling WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth on it) silently produces an instance with hash-collision protection disabled, weakening security when the copy is used for untrusted input.

receipt_plan.detail: Run CopyingUntrustedSecurityRetainsHashCollisionResistance: construct new MessagePackSecurity(MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData) and assert that HashCollisionResistant remains true. It fails on head because the property now retains its default value.
